name: Smoke Grenade keeps a split enemy attackable instead of dropping its aggro (#9837)
contract: witch_hunter_state::CanUnitAttack (AscensionWitchHunterDefenses.cpp) backs Unit::_IsValidAttackTarget, the single choke point both Spell::CheckCast's explicit hostile-target validation (SpellInfo::CheckExplicitTarget, spell non-null) and ThreatManager::ShouldBeOffline (via Creature::CanCreatureAttack -> IsValidAttackTarget, spell == nullptr) read. Returning false whenever InSmoke() was true regardless of the spell parameter made ThreatReference::UpdateOffline() mark a split enemy's threat reference offline and SendRemoveToClients it -- the reported 'drops aggro' symptom -- instead of only blocking the targeted cast/attack the tooltip promises ('enemies are unable to target into or out of the Smoke'). The fix only returns false for an actual spell-targeted check (spell != nullptr); the generic, spell-less check ThreatManager performs now stays true across the boundary, and an explicit hostile spell cast across it is still rejected exactly as before. The harness 'can_attack' metric calls IsValidAttackTarget(target, spell-or-null) directly, isolating both branches without needing live AI engagement.

steps.label: SETUP: the mob can attack the hunter before any smoke exists
SETUP: the hostile smoke cloud exists
SETUP: the mob (10.5 yd) is outside the 8 yd cloud, the hunter (its center) is inside
DISCRIMINATING: the split mob can still generically attack the hunter (ThreatManager's own check)
CONTROL: an explicit hostile spell cast across the same boundary is still rejected
